newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU countries resist farm aid cut plans.
newsitem.headline: EU countries resist farm aid cut plans.

text.p: European Union countries remain hostile to Commission proposals to make cuts in farm aids as part of the 1997/98 farm prices package, an EU member state official said on Wednesday.
"There can be no decision at next week's farm council but the Commission will make a report to ministers," the official said after a discussion by the EU's Special Committee on Agriculture.
Farm ministers meet in Luxembourg on April 21-22.
Opposition to the proposals to cut sugar storage aids, monthly cereals increments and arable area compensatory aids are opposed by most member states.
"The need for cuts is not accepted and most states expressed the view that agricultural spending should be taken right up the the annual limit," the official added.
In March, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler proposed a nine percent cut to 1.0 Ecus a tonne in the monthly increase in payments for cereals held in intervention stores.
Fischler also sought to cut the monthly sugar storage refund by 17 percent to 0.35 ecus per 100 kg.
Cereals and oilseeds compensatory payments would be cut by 7.3 percent and 4.2 percent respectively while set-aside payments would be slashed by 27 percent.
